hero_kpi_rationale: The Diabetes Care segment is Abbott's primary growth driver, fueled by the rising adoption of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) systems, a disruptive technology in diabetes management.

kpis.name: Diabetes Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) systems such as FreeStyle Libre.
kpis.description: Diabetes Care sales reached $7.6B in 2025, up 18.8% vs 2024 ($6.4B), driven by demand for CGM systems.
kpis.signal: Sustained double-digit growth driven by global CGM adoption.

kpis.name: Medical Devices Revenue Growth
kpis.explanation: Organic sales growth in the medical devices segment, excluding foreign exchange effects.
kpis.description: The Medical Devices segment grew sales by 11.9% in 2025, following +13.7% in 2024, supported by innovation and expanded indications.
kpis.signal: Double-digit growth across all sub-segments, particularly in cardiovascular and diabetes.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of goods sold, expressed as a percentage of net sales.
kpis.description: Gross margin reached 52.6% in 2025 (vs 50.9% in 2024 and 50.3% in 2023), reflecting favorable impacts from margin improvement initiatives.
kpis.signal: Expanding margin due to improvement initiatives, partially offset by costs and foreign exchange effects.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.description: Operating margin increased to 18.2% in 2025, compared to 16.3% in 2024 and 16.2% in 2023, a 1.9-point improvement.
kpis.signal: Ongoing improvement driven by efficiency initiatives and higher sales volumes.

kpis.name: R&D (as % of revenue)
kpis.explanation: Research and development expenses as a percentage of net revenue.
kpis.description: The R&D-to-revenue ratio stands at approximately 6.6% ($2.9B / $44.3B in net sales), comparable to leading medical device companies.
kpis.signal: Stable investment in medical innovation, with $2.9B spent on R&D in 2025.

kpis.name: Headcount (employees)
kpis.description: Abbott employs approximately 115,000 people, a stable workforce reflecting a controlled rationalization strategy.
kpis.signal: Stable headcount reflecting balanced human resource management despite inflationary pressures.

kpis.name: COVID-19 Testing Sales
kpis.explanation: Revenue related to COVID-19 diagnostic tests.
kpis.description: COVID-19-related sales declined to $297M in 2025, down from $747M in 2024 and $1.6B in 2023.
kpis.signal: Post-pandemic sales collapse, reflecting normalization of demand.

kpis.name: Emerging Markets Growth
kpis.explanation: Organic sales growth in emerging markets, representing 37% of total sales.
kpis.description: Sales in emerging markets increased by 5.1% in 2025 (excluding foreign exchange effects), after +8.2% in 2024, representing 37% of the company's total sales.
kpis.signal: Slowing but still positive growth in developing regions.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale.

risks.title: U.S. Tax Litigation
risks.score_rationale: Central position in the 10-K with multiple IRS SNODs (2017-2020) totaling over $1.5 billion. Firm language on contesting, but high risk if lost. 'Litigation' category heavily weighted here.

risks.title: Tax Assessment in Malaysia
risks.score_rationale: Mention of a $413 million assessment in 2024, upheld by court in October 2025. Abbott is appealing, but initial adverse ruling indicates tangible risk. Lower than U.S. litigation in overall scope.

risks.title: Impact of IVDR Regulation in Europe
risks.score_rationale: IVDR cited as imposing increased requirements with transition deadlines extending to 2029. Technical language but concerning for diagnostic product compliance. Major regulatory risk for the Diagnostics segment.

risks.title: Costly Operational Restructurings
risks.score_rationale: Restructuring charges of $274 million in 2025, impacting CoGS, R&D and SG&A. High and recurring amounts over 3 years. Language indicates significant rationalization efforts across Diagnostics, Nutritionals, Pharmaceutical Products and Medical Devices divisions.

risks.title: Risk from Global Minimum Tax (Pillar 2)
risks.score_rationale: OECD Pillar 2 mentioned, but potential exemption for U.S. groups announced in January 2026. Risk mitigated by this exemption, but monitoring ongoing. Language is cautious but not alarming.

risks.title: R&D Dependence Without Primary Research
risks.score_rationale: In established pharmaceutical products, Abbott does not conduct primary research, limiting breakthrough innovation. Moderate but structural risk, mentioned in the R&D process.

ai_positioning.summary: No significant mention of artificial intelligence was found in the 10-K.
